/// One value this run was given, above the defaults.
pub struct Given {
    /// What it sets.
    pub setting: &'static Setting,
    /// Where it came from, as typed: `--cookie`, or `$MY_APP_SESSIONS__COOKIE`.
    pub from: String,
    /// The value, as typed. Empty is `None` for an `Option` setting.
    pub value: String,
}

/// The name each flag answers to after `src/flags.rs`, whether the flags are
/// read or not.
///
/// A rename of a key no flag sets, a name that is not spelled as a flag, and
/// two flags under one name each stop the binary: each would otherwise be a
/// flag that does nothing, or does something else.
fn names() -> Result<Vec<(&'static Setting, &'static str)>, String> {
    let flags = || SETTINGS.iter().filter(|setting| setting.flag);
    for (path, _) in crate::flags::RENAMES {
        if !flags().any(|setting| setting.path == *path) {
            let known: Vec<&str> = flags().map(|setting| setting.path).collect();
            return Err(format!(
                "src/flags.rs renames `{path}`, and no flag sets it\nhelp: the flags are {}",
                known.join(", ")
            ));
        }
    }
    let mut names: Vec<(&'static Setting, &'static str)> = Vec::new();
    for setting in flags() {
        let name = crate::flags::RENAMES
            .iter()
            .find(|(path, _)| *path == setting.path)
            .map_or(setting.path, |(_, name)| *name);
        if name.is_empty() {
            continue;
        }
        let spelled = name
            .chars()
            .all(|c| c.is_ascii_lowercase() || c.is_ascii_digit() || "._-".contains(c));
        let taken = ["help", "version", "settings"].contains(&name);
        if !spelled || name.starts_with(['-', '.', '_']) || taken {
            return Err(format!(
                "src/flags.rs names a flag `{name}`\nhelp: a flag is lower case, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`, starts with a letter or a digit, and is not `help`, `version` or `settings`"
            ));
        }
        if let Some((other, _)) = names.iter().find(|(_, taken)| *taken == name) {
            return Err(format!(
                "`--{name}` would set both `{}` and `{}`\nhelp: rename one of them in src/flags.rs",
                other.path, setting.path
            ));
        }
        names.push((setting, name));
    }
    Ok(names)
}

/// The flags this run reads: none unless `src/flags.rs` turns them on,
/// because with a config file the file is the source.
pub fn flag_names() -> Result<Vec<(&'static Setting, &'static str)>, String> {
    if !crate::flags::WITH_CONFIG {
        return Ok(Vec::new());
    }
    names()
}

/// A flag given while the flags are off, refused by name with what to do
/// instead. Silently ignoring it would run with a value nobody chose.
pub fn refuse_off_flags() -> Result<(), String> {
    if crate::flags::WITH_CONFIG {
        return Ok(());
    }
    let names = names()?;
    for arg in std::env::args_os().skip(1) {
        let arg = arg.to_string_lossy();
        if arg == "--" {
            break;
        }
        let Some(written) = arg.strip_prefix("--") else {
            continue;
        };
        let name = written.split_once('=').map_or(written, |(name, _)| name);
        if let Some((setting, _)) = names.iter().find(|(_, known)| *known == name) {
            let (section, key) = setting.path.rsplit_once('.').unwrap_or(("", setting.path));
            return Err(format!(
                "`--{name}` is off: this project reads its settings from config/<env>.toml\nhelp: set WITH_CONFIG = true in src/flags.rs, or set `{key}` under [{section}] in config/<env>.toml"
            ));
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// The flags this run was given, in the order typed. The environment is not
/// here: `brocanth-config` reads it, under the file and over the flags.
///
/// `--name=VALUE` and `--name VALUE`. Every other argument is left alone: it
/// is a command's, and the command line's own parser has already refused what
/// nobody declared.
pub fn given() -> Result<Vec<Given>, String> {
    let mut given = Vec::new();
    let names = flag_names()?;
    let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args_os()
        .skip(1)
        .map(|arg| arg.to_string_lossy().into_owned())
        .collect();
    let mut rest = args.iter();
    while let Some(arg) = rest.next() {
        if arg == "--" {
            break;
        }
        let Some(written) = arg.strip_prefix("--") else {
            continue;
        };
        let (name, inline) = match written.split_once('=') {
            Some((name, value)) => (name, Some(value.to_string())),
            None => (written, None),
        };
        let Some((setting, name)) = names.iter().copied().find(|(_, known)| *known == name) else {
            continue;
        };
        let value = match inline {
            Some(value) => value,
            None => rest
                .next()
                .cloned()
                .ok_or_else(|| format!("--{name} needs a value\nhelp: write --{name}=VALUE"))?,
        };
        given.push(Given {
            setting,
            from: format!("--{name}"),
            value,
        });
    }
    Ok(given)
}

/// The configuration this run reads: the files, the environment, and the
/// flags on top once `src/flags.rs` turns them on.
pub fn config() -> Result<brocanth_config::Config, String> {
    refuse_off_flags()?;
    let mut loader = brocanth_config::Loader::new(crate::app::APP);
    for setting in SETTINGS {
        if let Some(alias) = setting.none_as {
            loader = loader.none_as(setting.path, alias);
        }
    }
    for given in given()? {
        let flag = given.from.trim_start_matches('-');
        loader = loader.flag(given.setting.path, flag, &given.value, given.setting.text);
    }
    loader.load().map_err(|e| e.to_string())
}

/// The flags, as arguments every command takes.
///
/// A name a command already takes is refused here: `clap` panics on it in a
/// debug build and lets one of the two win in a release one.
pub fn flag_args(
    command: brocanth_command::clap::Command,
) -> brocanth_command::anyhow::Result<brocanth_command::clap::Command> {
    use brocanth_command::{anyhow, clap};

    refuse_off_flags().map_err(anyhow::Error::msg)?;
    let mut command = command;
    for (setting, name) in flag_names().map_err(anyhow::Error::msg)? {
        let taken = command
            .get_subcommands()
            .flat_map(|sub| sub.get_arguments())
            .any(|arg| arg.get_long() == Some(name));
        if taken {
            anyhow::bail!(
                "`--{name}` sets `{}` and is also an argument of a command\nhelp: rename it in src/flags.rs",
                setting.path
            );
        }
        command = command.arg(
            clap::Arg::new(name)
                .long(name)
                .value_name("VALUE")
                .help(setting.help)
                .global(true)
                .action(clap::ArgAction::Append),
        );
    }
    Ok(command)
}

/// Each setting as the plugin's `Default` says, before any layer.
fn defaults() -> Vec<(&'static str, String)> {
    let gtag = brocanth_gtag::GtagConfig::default();
    vec![
        ("gtag.enabled", format!("{:?}", gtag.enabled)),
        ("gtag.measurement_id", format!("{:?}", gtag.measurement_id)),
        ("gtag.consent_mode", format!("{:?}", gtag.consent_mode)),
        ("gtag.respect_gpc", format!("{:?}", gtag.respect_gpc)),
        ("gtag.consent_days", format!("{:?}", gtag.consent_days)),
        ("gtag.send_title", format!("{:?}", gtag.send_title)),
        ("gtag.cookie_domain", format!("{:?}", gtag.cookie_domain)),
        ("gtag.consent_log", format!("{:?}", gtag.consent_log)),
        ("gtag.banner.text", format!("{:?}", gtag.banner.text)),
        ("gtag.banner.accept", format!("{:?}", gtag.banner.accept)),
        ("gtag.banner.refuse", format!("{:?}", gtag.banner.refuse)),
        ("gtag.banner.manage", format!("{:?}", gtag.banner.manage)),
        (
            "gtag.banner.policy_url",
            format!("{:?}", gtag.banner.policy_url),
        ),
    ]
}

/// Every settings layer on its own, lowest first, then the merged values.
/// A secret is masked in every layer.
pub fn settings_report() -> Result<String, String> {
    let config = config()?;
    let mut layers = config.layers().defaults(defaults());
    for setting in SETTINGS.iter().filter(|setting| !setting.flag) {
        layers = layers.secret(setting.path);
    }
    Ok(layers.to_string())
}

/// `[server] shutdown_grace_secs`, or
/// [`SHUTDOWN_GRACE`](crate::app::SHUTDOWN_GRACE) when it is not set.
pub fn shutdown_grace() -> Result<std::time::Duration, String> {
    let config = brocanth_config::Loader::new(crate::app::APP)
        .load()
        .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    let Some(value) = config
        .raw_section("server")
        .and_then(|server| server.get("shutdown_grace_secs"))
    else {
        return Ok(crate::app::SHUTDOWN_GRACE);
    };
    // An integer in a file, and a string in `$MY_BLOG_SERVER__SHUTDOWN_GRACE_SECS`.
    value
        .as_integer()
        .and_then(|secs| u64::try_from(secs).ok())
        .or_else(|| value.as_str().and_then(|secs| secs.trim().parse().ok()))
        .map(std::time::Duration::from_secs)
        .ok_or_else(|| {
            format!(
                "`[server] shutdown_grace_secs` is {}, and it must be a whole number of seconds",
                value.display()
            )
        })
}

/// What the server is handed for one request.
pub type Answer = brocanth::plugin_routes::BoxFuture<'static, brocanth_server::Response>;

/// What `serve` answers a request with: `next`, as it is. `brocanth add
/// observe` logs and counts each request here, and answers the probes.
pub fn wrap<F, Fut>(
    app: &std::sync::Arc<crate::app::App>,
    next: F,
) -> impl Fn(brocanth_server::Request) -> Answer + Send + Sync + 'static
where
    F: Fn(brocanth_server::Request) -> Fut + Send + Sync + 'static,
    Fut: std::future::Future<Output = brocanth_server::Response> + Send + 'static,
{
    let _ = app;
    move |request| -> Answer { Box::pin(next(request)) }
}

/// No second listener: nothing here serves probes or metrics.
pub async fn side_listeners(app: &crate::app::App) -> Result<(), String> {
    let _ = app;
    Ok(())
}

/// The first half of a stop: the listener closes at once.
pub async fn stop_accepting(app: &crate::app::App, stopper: brocanth_server::Stopper) {
    let _ = app;
    stopper.stop();
}

// brocanth-digest: 6f72d30f2cc07e8a
===== src/flags.rs =====
//! The command-line flags of this binary, and the one place to rename them.
//!
//! A module declares each of its settings once. From that the binary takes a
//! flag, `--<module>.<key>=VALUE`, an environment variable,
//! `$<APP>_<MODULE>__<KEY>`, and, with the `config` module, a key in
//! `config/<env>.toml`. `brocanth add` rewrites the list in
//! `src/plugins/mod.rs`. This file is yours: it is written when it is missing
//! and never again.

/// Whether a project with a config file reads the flags too.
///
/// Off: with the `config` module, the file and the environment are the
/// sources, and a flag is refused with a pointer to this line. On: a flag
/// outranks both, for one run. Without the `config` module the flags are
/// always read, and this is not.
#[allow(dead_code)]
pub const WITH_CONFIG: bool = false;

/// Flags under another name: the key as the module declares it, and the flag
/// this binary answers to instead, without `--`. An empty name hides the
/// flag.
///
/// ```text
/// ("sessions.cookie", "cookie"),
/// ("storage.root", ""),
/// ```
pub const RENAMES: &[(&str, &str)] = &[];
===== config/development.toml =====
# The configuration of this environment.
#
# The framework owns `[app]` and `[server]`. Every other section is claimed by
# the plugin instance registered under that name in src/main.rs, and a section
# nothing claims stops the build rather than being silently ignored -- a
# misspelt section must never build clean.
#
# Layered, highest precedence first: $MY_BLOG_CONFIG, /etc/my_blog/development.toml,
# ./my_blog_development.toml, ./config/development.toml. $MY_BLOG_ENV picks the
# environment; without it, development.

[app]
name = "My Blog"

[server]
# Seconds a stop (SIGTERM or Ctrl-C) waits for open requests, then for the
# plugins. Keep it below the orchestrator's kill timeout: Kubernetes waits 30.
shutdown_grace_secs = 25

[gtag]
# Insert the consent banner and the Google tag into every HTML page.
# Off outside production, so a developer's visits are not counted.
enabled = false
# The GA4 measurement id, `G-` then capitals and digits.
measurement_id = ""
# `basic`: no Google script before consent. `advanced`: cookieless pings before it.
consent_mode = "basic"
# Treat Global Privacy Control and Do Not Track as a refusal.
respect_gpc = true
# How long a choice is kept before the banner asks again, in days.
# Six months is what the CNIL recommends.
consent_days = 182
# Send the page title. Off: the scrubbed path stands in for it.
send_title = false
# The query parameters that reach Google; every other one is removed.
allow_params = ["utm_source", "utm_medium", "utm_campaign", "utm_term", "utm_content"]
# Paths that never get the tag, each with everything under it.
exclude = ["/admin"]
# The domain Google's cookies live on, such as `example.co.uk`. Empty: the tag picks it. Empty means none.
# cookie_domain = ""
# A file each consent choice is appended to, such as `log/consent.jsonl`. Empty: none. Empty means none.
# A server only: a static export has no one to report a choice to.
# consent_log = ""

[gtag.banner]
# The sentence the banner asks with.
text = "We would like to measure visits with Google Analytics. It sets cookies only if you accept."
# The button that accepts.
accept = "Accept"
# The button that refuses.
refuse = "Refuse"
# The button that opens the banner again.
manage = "Cookie settings"
# A link to the privacy policy, such as `/privacy`. Empty means no link. Empty means none.
# policy_url = ""

===== src/commands/serve.rs =====
//! `serve` -- the one command the scaffold wrote.
//!
//! It is ordinary project code: rename it, give it more flags, or delete it.
//! The framework does not own this command line.

use brocanth_command::{anyhow, clap, cmd, Command, Context};

/// Serve the application over HTTP.
#[cmd]
#[derive(clap::Args)]
pub struct Serve {
    /// Address to bind.
    #[arg(long, default_value_t = crate::app::default_addr())]
    pub addr: String,
}

impl Command for Serve {
    fn run(self, _ctx: &mut Context) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
        crate::app::serve(&self.addr).map_err(anyhow::Error::msg)
    }
}
===== src/commands/settings.rs =====
//! `settings` -- every settings layer on its own, then the merged values.
//!
//! Ordinary project code, like `serve`: rename it or delete it, and delete
//! its line in `src/commands/mod.rs`.

use brocanth_command::{anyhow, clap, cmd, Command, Context};

/// Show each settings layer, lowest precedence first, then the merged values.
#[cmd]
#[derive(clap::Args)]
pub struct Settings {}

impl Command for Settings {
    fn run(self, _ctx: &mut Context) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
        print!(
            "{}",
            crate::plugins::settings_report().map_err(anyhow::Error::msg)?
        );
        Ok(())
    }
}
===== .github/workflows/ci.yml =====
# Every push and every pull request: formatting, lints, tests.
#
# The toolchain is the one `rust-toolchain.toml` pins. A dependency on a path
# outside this repository (`brocanth create --brocanth-path`) is not in the
# checkout, and the build fails; depend on git instead.
name: ci

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always

jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      # Reads rust-toolchain.toml, and caches the target directory.
      - uses: actions-rust-lang/setup-rust-toolchain@v1
        with:
          components: rustfmt, clippy
      - run: cargo fmt --all --check
      - run: cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
      - run: cargo test
      - run: cargo run -- export
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: site
          path: dist
===== assets/css/_tailwind.css =====
/* The input of the CSS build. Never published.
 *
 * The leading underscore marks an input: a file that is bundled into another
 * and that `assets!` must not publish on its own. The build reads this file
 * and writes assets/css/site.css, which is the one that ships:
 *
 *     brocanth css          # once, minified
 *     brocanth css -W       # again on each change
 */

@import "tailwindcss";

/* Where the class names are.
 *
 * Tailwind resolves each path against this stylesheet and keeps its automatic
 * detection on as well. These are explicit for two reasons: `.rsx` is not an
 * extension Tailwind knows, and an explicit glob states the contract.
 */

/* The templates. A .rsx file is Rust with an HTML-shaped body. */
@source "../../src/pages/**/*.rsx";

/* Plain Rust holds class names too -- a helper that builds a class string,
 * or a handler choosing one. */
@source "../../src/**/*.rs";

   `brocanth css` replaces it with the real one. */

===== src/assets.rs =====
//! Every static file this binary serves.
//!
//! Two directories, two rules. `assets/` is **fingerprinted** -- `site.css`
//! is published at `/css/site.<hash>.css`, so it can be cached forever and a
//! new build invalidates it by having a different name. `public/` is served
//! **verbatim**, because `robots.txt`, `favicon.ico` and anything linked to
//! from outside must keep the name they were given.
//!
//! Write a reference with `assets::url`, never by hand:
//!
//! ```ignore
//! <link rel="stylesheet" href={assets::url("css/site.css")}>
//! ```
//!
//! A name nothing publishes panics there rather than 404ing in a browser.
//!
//! Embedded, like the templates and the route table, so `serve` works from
//! any directory and nothing can go missing after the build passed. A file
//! added where there was none needs `touch src/assets.rs`, because nothing
//! referenced it yet.

brocanth_assets::assets!("assets", "public");
===== src/commands/css.rs =====
//! `css` -- build assets/css/site.css from assets/css/_tailwind.css.
//!
//!     brocanth css          once, minified
//!     brocanth css -W       again on each change
//!
//! Ordinary project code, like `serve`: rename it, give it more flags, or
//! delete it. It is here rather than in a shell script because this project
//! already has a command line, and a second way to run things is a second
//! thing to keep in step.
//!
//! The Tailwind CLI comes out of `node_modules` and there is no fallback to
//! `npx`. A fallback downloads some other version and hides the one fact
//! worth knowing, which is that nobody ran `npm install`.

use std::path::Path;
use std::process::Command as Child;

use brocanth_command::{anyhow, clap, cmd, Command, Context};

/// Build the stylesheet from the Tailwind input.
#[cmd]
#[derive(clap::Args)]
pub struct Css {
    /// Rebuild on each change instead of once.
    #[arg(short = 'W', long)]
    pub watch: bool,
}

const INPUT: &str = "assets/css/_tailwind.css";
const OUTPUT: &str = "assets/css/site.css";
const CLI: &str = "node_modules/.bin/tailwindcss";

impl Command for Css {
    fn run(self, ctx: &mut Context) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
        // The project root and not the working directory: `brocanth css`
        // runs from wherever you happen to be, and every path below is
        // written relative to the project.
        let root = ctx.root();
        let cli = root.join(CLI);
        if !cli.is_file() {
            anyhow::bail!(
                "the Tailwind CLI is absent at {}\n       run `npm install` in {} first",
                cli.display(),
                root.display()
            );
        }

        let mut child = Child::new(&cli);
        child
            .current_dir(root)
            .args(["--input", INPUT, "--output", OUTPUT]);
        if self.watch {
            child.arg("--watch");
        } else {
            child.arg("--minify");
        }

        let status = child.status()?;
        if !status.success() {
            // No message beyond this: the CLI has already written its own
            // on the stderr this process inherited.
            anyhow::bail!("the Tailwind CLI failed");
        }

        // `--watch` only ever returns when it was interrupted, and the
        // output it leaves behind is whatever the last change produced.
        // Checking it, or touching the module below, would both be about a
        // build that is over.
        if self.watch {
            return Ok(());
        }

        let written = root.join(OUTPUT);
        let bytes = std::fs::metadata(&written)?.len();
        if bytes == 0 {
            anyhow::bail!("the build wrote no CSS to {}", written.display());
        }

        touch(&root.join("src/assets.rs"))?;
        println!("built {OUTPUT} ({bytes} bytes)");
        Ok(())
    }
}

/// Make cargo notice a stylesheet it has already compiled in.
///
/// The CSS is embedded at compile time, so a new one is a new binary, and
/// nothing rebuilds until the module that embeds it looks newer than the
/// artefact. Rewriting its own bytes is the portable way to say so: there is
/// no `utimes` in `std`, and a dependency for one call is not worth it.
fn touch(path: &Path) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
    let same = std::fs::read(path)?;
    std::fs::write(path, same)?;
    Ok(())
}
===== src/commands/export.rs =====
//! `export` -- the site, as files.
//!
//! `brocanth-static` does the work. Every route that answers GET is
//! requested once, through the same `handle` that `serve` uses, and its
//! answer is written under `--out`. A page at `/about` becomes
//! `about/index.html`, so `/about` works on any static host. A route whose
//! last segment has a dot (`/feed.xml`) is written under its own name.
//! Every embedded asset is written at the path it is published at, and the
//! 404 page is `404.html`.
//!
//! `--base /my-site` prefixes every root-relative URL in the pages, for a
//! site served under a path, such as a GitHub Pages project site.
//!
//! This file is yours. Add the paths of routes with parameters to `PATHS`.
//! Set `PARTIALS` to the most layout layers a page has to write the
//! partials dp-swap's `partialDir` reads.

use std::path::PathBuf;

use brocanth_command::{anyhow, clap, cmd, Command, Context};

/// The concrete paths of routes with a parameter. The export cannot guess
/// which ids exist, so a route like `/users/{id}` is written only for the
/// paths listed here.
const PATHS: &[&str] = &["/users/7"];

/// One partial per layout depth, `1..=PARTIALS`, under `partials/<depth>/`.
/// `0` writes documents only.
const PARTIALS: u32 = 0;

/// Write the site to a directory any static host can serve.
#[cmd]
#[derive(clap::Args)]
pub struct Export {
    /// Directory to write. Emptied first.
    #[arg(long, default_value = "dist")]
    pub out: PathBuf,
    /// The path the site is served under, such as `/my-site`. Empty for
    /// the root of a domain.
    #[arg(long, default_value = "")]
    pub base: String,
}

impl Command for Export {
    fn run(self, _ctx: &mut Context) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
        let runtime = tokio::runtime::Builder::new_current_thread()
            .enable_all()
            .build()?;
        let app = {
            let _guard = runtime.enter();
            crate::app::build().map_err(anyhow::Error::msg)?
        };

        let site = brocanth_static::Export::new(&self.out)
            .base(&self.base)
            .partials(PARTIALS)
            .routes(&app.router)
            .paths(PATHS.iter().copied())
            .assets(
                crate::assets::ASSETS
                    .iter()
                    .map(|asset| (asset.published, asset.body)),
            );
        let report = runtime.block_on(site.run(|request| crate::app::handle(&app, request)))?;

        eprintln!("export: {report} in {}", self.out.display());
        for pattern in &report.skipped {
            eprintln!(
                "export: {pattern} has a parameter: only the paths in PATHS in src/commands/export.rs are written"
            );
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}
===== src/commands/routes.rs =====
//! Every route this application answers.
//!
//! `brocanth routes` builds this project and runs this command, so the
//! listing is the binary's own answer rather than a second reading of the
//! directory. The rows are `crate::pages::handlers()`, read off `src/pages`
//! while the crate compiled: a route is a file, so there is nothing to
//! regenerate and nothing that can fall behind.
//!
//! ```text
//! $ brocanth routes
//! VERB    PATTERN        HANDLER
//! GET     /              pages::index::handle
//! GET     /about         pages::about::handle
//! POST    /signup        pages::signup::handle_post
//! ```
//!
//! An argument keeps the rows that contain it, in any column, so
//! `routes signup` is the one page and `routes POST` is every route that
//! writes.
//!
//! These are the pages. A plugin that mounts its own routes through a
//! `RouteSource` would not be in the list, and nothing this project has
//! mounts one -- so today the two are the same table. Say so here if that
//! stops being true.

use brocanth_command::{anyhow, clap, cmd, Command, Context};

/// List the routes this application answers.
#[cmd]
#[derive(clap::Args)]
pub struct Routes {
    /// Keep only the rows containing this text
    pub filter: Option<String>,
}

impl Command for Routes {
    fn run(self, _ctx: &mut Context) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
        let (header, mut rows) = table();
        if let Some(filter) = &self.filter {
            rows.retain(|row| row.iter().any(|cell| cell.contains(filter)));
        }
        if rows.is_empty() {
            // An application with no page and a filter that matched nothing
            // both print nothing, and only one of the two is the reader's
            // own doing.
            match &self.filter {
                Some(filter) => println!("no route matches `{filter}`"),
                None => println!("this application answers no route"),
            }
            return Ok(());
        }

        let mut widths: Vec<usize> = header.iter().map(|title| title.chars().count()).collect();
        for row in &rows {
            for (column, cell) in row.iter().enumerate() {
                widths[column] = widths[column].max(cell.chars().count());
            }
        }

        print_row(&widths, header.iter().copied());
        for row in &rows {
            print_row(&widths, row.iter().map(String::as_str));
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

/// One line, every cell padded to its column but the last.
///
/// The last is left alone, because trailing spaces are invisible until
/// something pipes this into a diff.
fn print_row<'a>(widths: &[usize], cells: impl Iterator<Item = &'a str>) {
    let mut line = String::new();
    for (column, cell) in cells.enumerate() {
        if column > 0 {
            line.push_str("  ");
        }
        if column + 1 == widths.len() {
            line.push_str(cell);
        } else {
            line.push_str(&format!("{cell:<width$}", width = widths[column]));
        }
    }
    println!("{line}");
}

/// The header, and one row per route.
///
/// Three columns: a route is a verb, a pattern, and the function that
/// answers it. What each one takes and gives would be a fourth and a fifth,
/// and they arrive with the `input` module -- without it nothing in this
/// project has read a handler's signature.
fn table() -> (Vec<&'static str>, Vec<Vec<String>>) {
    let rows = crate::pages::handlers()
        .iter()
        .map(|(verb, pattern, handler)| {
            vec![
                verb.as_str().to_string(),
                (*pattern).to_string(),
                format!("pages::{handler}"),
            ]
        })
        .collect();
    (vec!["VERB", "PATTERN", "HANDLER"], rows)
}
===== src/pages/about.rsx =====
// The parameters are this page's contract with its handler. Rename one and
// src/pages/about.rs stops compiling, which is the point.

pub fn About(title: &str, verb: &str, path: &str) -> Element {
    <h1>About</h1>
    <p>
        You asked for <code>{verb} {path}</code>. This page answers GET
        and nothing else, so a DELETE to it is a 405 carrying
        an <code>Allow</code> header rather than a 404.
    </p>
    <p>The shell around this is <code>src/pages/layout.rsx</code>, which {title} shares with every page.</p>
}
===== src/pages/index.rsx =====
use crate::pages::views::link::Link;

// The page, and only the page. The document around it is layout.rsx, and
// this file does not know it exists.

pub fn Index(title: &str) -> Element {
    <h1>{title}</h1>
    <p>
        This file is <code>src/pages/index.rsx</code>, beside the handler
        in <code>index.rs</code>, and it is compiled into the binary. Edit it
        and cargo rebuilds; break it and the build stops on the line you broke.
    </p>
    <p>
        An interpolated value is escaped on the way out, always. Writing
        markup verbatim needs a different and greppable hole, so an injection
        is something you can search for rather than something you have to
        remember.
    </p>
    <ul>
        <li><Link to="/about">/about</Link></li>
        <li><Link to={&crate::pages::routes::users::id::path(7)}>User 7</Link></li>
    </ul>
}
===== src/pages/layout.rsx =====
// The document every page in this directory, and every directory below it,
// is rendered inside. A page never names it: which layout wraps a page is a
// property of where the page is, which is the rule the Crystal page_router
// uses for layout.cr.
//
// A layout is an ordinary component with a parameter of type `Element`, and
// `children` is the only parameter `html!` fills -- it cannot know what a
// second one would mean. A value every page shares comes from a const, as
// the title does here; a value belonging to one request belongs on the page
// component, which the handler builds and which already has the context.

use crate::pages::TITLE;

pub fn Layout(layout: &str, children: Element) -> Element {
    <!DOCTYPE html>
    <html lang="en">
        <head>
            <meta charset="utf-8">
            <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
            <title>{TITLE}</title>
            <link rel="stylesheet" href={crate::assets::url("css/site.css")}>
            <script src={crate::assets::url("dpswap.min.js")} defer></script>
        </head>
        <body class="min-h-screen bg-white text-slate-900">
            <header><a href="/">{TITLE}</a></header>
            <main dp-layout={layout} id="outlet">{children}</main>
        </body>
    </html>
}
===== src/pages/link.rsx =====
// An anchor that swaps instead of reloading the document.
//
// Written as a real <a href> and enhanced afterwards. With JavaScript off,
// to a crawler, and on the first load of any page it is a link and the
// browser does what it always did -- which is why `to` is required and why
// there is no version of this that renders a <span> with a click handler.
//
// `to` takes what the route helpers return:
//
//     <Link to={routes::users::id::path(7)}>User 7</Link>
//
// never a string. A route that does not exist is then a compile error
// rather than a 404 somebody finds later.

pub fn Link(to: &str, children: Element) -> Element {
    <a href={to} dp-boost>{children}</a>
}
===== src/pages/users/[id].rsx =====
// Two layouts wrap this one: the root, and users/layout.rsx beside it.
// Neither is named here or anywhere else -- `html!` reads the directory
// tree. Delete users/layout.rsx and this page is wrapped in one.

pub fn User(id: u64) -> Element {
    <h1>User {id}</h1>
    <p>
        The <code>id</code> came out of the path. A component takes typed
        parameters, so this one is a <code>u64</code> the whole way
        from <code>src/pages/users/[id].rs</code>, never a string that
        might not be a number.
    </p>
}
===== src/pages/users/layout.rsx =====
// Wraps every page under src/pages/users/, inside the root layout rather
// than instead of it. Nothing declares the stacking: `html!` reads it off
// the directory tree.
//
// `layout` is the URL prefix this layout covers, filled in by `html!`, and
// `dp-layout` is the marker dp-swap walks to find the deepest layer two
// pages share. It goes on the element wrapping exactly the children and
// nothing else: anything inside it is replaced along with them, so a
// sidebar in here would lose its scroll position on every navigation.

pub fn Layout(layout: &str, children: Element) -> Element {
    <section class="users">
        <nav><a href="/">home</a></nav>
        <div dp-layout={layout}>{children}</div>
    </section>
}
===== AGENTS.md =====
<!-- Written by `brocanth`. Do not edit -- `brocanth add` rewrites this file. -->
<!-- Notes of your own go in a file of your own, beside this one. -->
# Working in My Blog

A brief for a coding agent. Written by `brocanth`, so the lists
below are this project's and not the framework's in general.

## Check your work

Run these after every change, in this order. They are ordered by how
fast they fail.

```
cargo test
cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo fmt --check
```

The route table is `pages::router()` and the test beside it asserts the
shape of the directory. Read it rather than guessing what covers a
request.

## What this binary contains

- `core`  the router, the context, the plugin seams
- `static`  `export` writes every GET page and every asset to dist/; no server, so no runtime modules
- `config`  config/<env>.toml, merged; without it nothing links a TOML parser
- `commands`  this project's own command line, `serve` plus whatever you add
- `rsx`  `.rsx` templates compiled into the binary; without it a page builds a String
- `rsx-tailwind`  a CSS build over the class names in your templates; needs node
- `rsx-htmx`  a click swaps what changed; the server renders from the shared layout down
- `ci`  fmt, clippy and the tests on every push; pick the provider below
- `ci-github`  .github/workflows/ci.yml: fmt, clippy, tests, a Postgres service when there is a database, the image
- `gtag`  Google Analytics 4 behind a consent banner; nothing leaves before the visitor accepts

**Absent:** `logging`, `observability`, `observability-logs`, `observability-health`, `observability-metrics`, `observability-tracing`, `analytics`, `beacon`, `sessions`, `db`, `model`, `cache`, `jobs`, `auth`, `policy`, `storage`, `input`, `client`, `middleware`, `middleware-csrf`, `middleware-security-headers`, `middleware-rate-limit`, `openapi`, `validation`, `resource`, `admin`, `admin-model`, `realtime`, `realtime-sse`, `jt`, `robots`, `docker`, `docker-kubernetes` — not compiled, not linked, absent from `Cargo.lock`. Do not write code that uses them; add the dependency and name the plugin in `main` first.

That is the framework's central rule: a capability nobody asked for is
not compiled and not linked. If you need one, add it to `Cargo.toml`
*and* name its plugin in `src/main.rs`. Nothing registers itself.

## Adding a route

A route is a file. `src/pages/about.rs` is `/about`;
`src/pages/users/[id].rs` is `/users/{id}`. **Write the file. That is
the whole of it** -- no `mod` line, no row to register, because there is
no list. `brocanth_pages::pages!` in `src/pages/mod.rs` reads this
directory while the crate compiles and writes both.

The verb comes off the handler's name: `handle` is GET, then
`handle_head`, `handle_post`, `handle_put`, `handle_patch`,
`handle_delete`, `handle_options`. A `pub fn handle_*` outside that
list is a build error naming the list, rather than a handler nothing
reaches; a page with no handler is a build error too. A private
`fn handle_*` is a helper and is left alone.

A handler may be `pub async fn` when it waits on something, such as a
database: the table awaits it and the wait holds no thread. A page that
waits on nothing stays a plain `fn`. An async handler is dropped at an
`.await` when the client goes away, so do not leave a write half done
across one.

**Adding a file does not rebuild on its own** -- nothing referenced it
yet. Run `touch src/pages/mod.rs` after creating a page or a layout.
Editing or deleting one is noticed.

A handler returns a value and never writes a response itself. That is
what makes a half-written body on an error impossible rather than
unlikely.

## Views

The markup for a route is a `.rsx` file **next to the page that renders it**:
`src/pages/index.rsx` beside `src/pages/index.rs`. There is no second tree and
nothing to register -- `rsx::load_dir!("src/pages")` in `src/pages/mod.rs`
compiles them all into the binary. One file is one module, under `views`, so
`index.rsx` is `views::index` and `users/[id].rsx` is `views::users::_id_`.

### Layouts

`layout.rsx` wraps every page in its directory **and every directory below**,
and a page never names it: which layout wraps a page is a property of where
the page is. That is the Crystal page_router's rule for `layout.cr`.

They stack root to leaf, and **the chain is not written down anywhere**.
`html!` is a macro: it knows which file it was written in, walks up to
`src/`, and wraps the page in every `layout.rsx` it passes. So
`src/pages/users/layout.rsx` wraps the pages under `users/` inside the root
layout, and deleting that file removes exactly that layer with no other edit.

Every page uses the same import and the same call, whatever directory it is
in. Do not add a chain of your own; if a page is wrapped wrongly, the
directory tree is what to change.

A layout takes `children: Element`, and may also take `layout: &str`, which
`html!` fills with the URL prefix that layout covers. Those two are the only
parameters it fills, because it cannot know what a third one would mean.
A value every page shares comes from a `const` -- the root layout reads
`pages::TITLE` that way. A value belonging to one request belongs on the page
component, which the handler builds and which already has the context.

For a fragment that is not a document -- an htmx swap, a partial -- call
`render` instead of `html!`: the same thing with no shell.

**Adding a `layout.rsx` where there was none does not rebuild anything**,
because nothing referenced the file yet. Run `touch src/pages/mod.rs` after
creating one. Editing or deleting an existing layout is noticed.

A component is a function returning `Element`. Its parameters are its contract
with the handler, and a caller fills them as struct fields, so a field the
component does not declare is a compile error rather than a blank in the page.
A parameter of type `Element` receives children, which is all a layout is.

Reach a template from a handler with `html!`, and with nothing else:

```rust
pub fn handle(_ctx: &mut Ctx) -> Result<impl IntoResponse, Error> {
    html!(ctx, views::index::Index { title: TITLE })
}
```

It returns the handler's own `Result`, so there is no `Ok(..)` to write and a
template that bails propagates with `?`. For another status or a header,
compose with the other return shapes: `Ok((html!(ctx, tpl)?, 404))`.

Adding a page with markup is two files in one directory -- `<name>.rs` and
`<name>.rsx` -- and nothing else anywhere. Neither needs a line in
`src/pages/mod.rs`, because the directory is the registry.

Not every response is a page. A redirect is `Response::empty(303)` with a
header and no template anywhere near it.

An interpolated value is escaped on the way out. Templates are read at
**compile** time, so an edit needs a rebuild, and a template that does not
parse is a build failure on its own line rather than a 500.

## Static files

Two directories, and the difference matters. `assets/` is **fingerprinted**:
`site.css` is published at `/css/site.<hash>.css` and cached for a year.
`public/` is served **verbatim**, for names that cannot move -- `robots.txt`,
`favicon.ico`, anything linked to from outside.

Never write either URL by hand. `crate::assets::url("css/site.css")` takes the
logical path and returns the published one, and a name nothing publishes
panics there rather than 404ing in a browser.

A basename starting with `_` is an input and is never published, which is what
`assets/css/_tailwind.css` is.

Both directories are embedded in the binary. **Adding a file where there was
none does not rebuild anything**; run `touch src/assets.rs` after creating one.

## Partial navigation

Link to a route with the `Link` component, never a bare `<a>`:

```
<Link to={&crate::pages::routes::users::id::path(7)}>User 7</Link>
```

`to` takes what a route helper returns, so a link to a route that does not
exist is a compile error. It renders a real `<a href>` with `dp-boost` on it,
so the page still works with no JavaScript.

A layout marks what a swap may replace with `dp-layout={layout}`, on the
element wrapping **exactly** the children. Anything inside that element is
replaced with them, so a sidebar or a scroll position belongs outside it.

A request carrying `DP-Partial: n` drops the outermost `n` layouts, and
`html!` resolves that into a `match` over the chain. A handler never reads the
header and never changes for it.

## Tasks

A command is a `clap::Args` struct with `#[cmd]` on it, in its own file under
`src/commands/`, plus a `pub mod` line at the end of `src/commands/mod.rs`,
below the line that starts `// Your commands`. `brocanth add` rewrites the
lines above it and keeps yours. The command becomes a subcommand
automatically — registration happens at link time.

```
brocanth --help      # lists this project's commands too
brocanth serve
brocanth css         # the CSS build; -W rebuilds on each change
```

The stylesheet is embedded, so a new one is a new binary. `css` rewrites
`src/assets.rs` to say so, which is what makes cargo notice.

## Decisions that belong to the person

The modules in this project are the person's choice. Do not add or
remove one on your own. Before you run `brocanth add`, show the person
the question: `brocanth add --questions` lists each module with its
default, what it needs and what it recommends. Give your
recommendation, and wait for the answer.

## House style

- A comment says **why**, next to the decision, and what was chosen
  against. Not what the line does.
- A test name is a sentence describing the guarantee it protects.
- Prefer a type that cannot be built wrong over a check that can be
  forgotten.
- State a limit where someone would look for it rather than leaving it
  to be discovered.

## Framework reference

`docs/llm-authoring.md` in the brocanth checkout is the full brief: what
cannot compile and can therefore be relied on, what can still go wrong
and therefore needs a test, and the crate map.

## Google Analytics

`brocanth_gtag::Gtag` is registered in `src/plugins/mod.rs`.
Its hook puts a consent banner and Google's tag into every HTML page,
before `</body>`. Nothing reaches Google before the visitor accepts.

Do not add a second Google tag, and do not send a page view yourself:
the hook scrubs the URL first. Never put an email address, a name or a
user id in a URL, a page title or an event: Google's terms forbid it,
and the scrubber only catches what it can recognise. A link with
`data-consent-manage` reopens the banner.

The choice lives in the visitor's browser. To keep a record of it on
the server, set `consent_log` to a file: each choice is one JSON line
with no address and no user agent.

## Static site

This project compiles to files. `cargo run -- export` writes every
route that answers GET to `dist/`, and every asset beside it. `serve`
is the preview, not the deployment.

- A page must answer the same bytes whatever the request says. It must
  not read a cookie or the query: the export sends none. The one
  header it sends is `DP-Partial`, for the partials (`PARTIALS`).
- A route with a parameter (`users/[id].rs`) is written only for the
  paths listed in `PATHS` in `src/commands/export.rs`. Add each one.
- Served under a path (a GitHub Pages project site)? Export with
  `cargo run -- export --base /<repo>`. Write links from the root
  (`/about`); the export prefixes them.
- Do not add a module that runs in a server (a session, a database, a
  queue, the observability probes). `brocanth add` refuses it.
